summary_paragraph: A 52-year-old female with systemic lupus erythematosus and end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis was admitted for one week of right shoulder pain and low-grade fever. Imaging showed changes consistent with early avascular necrosis, and joint aspiration revealed elevated white blood cells with no crystals, raising concern for septic arthritis despite negative cultures. She was started on IV vancomycin, with significant improvement in pain and function. Blood and fluid cultures remained negative, and lupus serologies were stable, supporting infection over flare. She was discharged home on a two-week course of vancomycin administered with dialysis and a single dose of fluconazole for a concurrent yeast infection. Follow-up was arranged with primary care, rheumatology, and orthopedics.
problems: Aseptic necrosis of head of humerus
